title: From the PRF bytes, or the recovery code, to the plaintext
caption: Section 8.2 of the brief as a picture. Two roots, one KEK: each unlock method derives its own wrapping key and the keyring holds one wrapped copy of the KEK per method, so adding a passkey adds a wrap and never re-encrypts the body. Red is secret and never stored; blue is public and stored in the clear; grey is derived in memory and thrown away.

items.label: PRF output, 32 bytes
items.detail: from the authenticator, per passkey, never stored

items.label: Recovery code, 128 bits
items.detail: 26 base32 characters, shown once, kept by you

items.label: prfSalt, 32 bytes
items.detail: in keyring.json, in the clear; the input, not a secret

items.label: WK_passkey (AES-256-GCM)
items.detail: one per passkey; in memory for the unlock

items.label: WK_recovery (AES-256-GCM)
items.detail: in memory, only during a recovery

items.label: KEK, 32 random bytes
items.detail: stored only as wraps[].ct, once per unlock method

items.label: The body: entries and the key pair
items.detail: stored only as body.ct; plaintext in memory, briefly
